prompt: Return a new list with duplicates removed, keeping only the FIRST occurrence of each string and preserving the original order.
explanation: Walking the list front to back and skipping anything already seen keeps exactly the first occurrence of each value. A HashSet gives constant-time membership checks, and its add method conveniently returns false when the element was already present, so one call both tests and records. Using result.contains(item) instead of a set also works but rescans the result list every time.
hints: Walk the input in order and only append strings you have not seen before.
A HashSet<String> remembers what you have already added; contains/add check membership fast.
HashSet.add returns false if the element was already in the set -- perfect inside an if.
